name: MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test Database: Robust Arrhythmia Benchmark
description: The MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test Database is a standardized stress-testing resource created by the MIT and Beth Israel Hospital biomedical engineering teams to quantitatively evaluate ECG arrhythmia detection algorithms under adverse noise conditions. It consists of 12 half-hour standard two-channel ECG recordings synthesized by combining clean recordings from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database with calibrated levels of realistic ambulatory noise (baseline wander, muscle tremor, and electrode motion artifact) at signal-to-noise ratios ranging from -6 dB to 24 dB. It also includes 3 pure half-hour recordings of typical clinical noise recorded from limbs using standard electrodes.
